text.p: Copper failed to hold above $1,900 and aluminium struck a fresh 2-1/4 year low overnight as metal markets continued to wobble but gold bullion firmed in New York.
Wheat futures were mixed but oil prices surged as the approaching northern hemisphere winter drove up heating oil prices. The CRB index closed 1.2 points higher at 245.84.

Three months aluminium dived to a fresh 2-1/4 year low of $1,340 in the morning but clawed its way up to close at $1,352, a $25 loss, on trade buying, mostly from the Far East. "I'm not convinced it's enough to keep it up," a trader said. Next major support was pegged around $1,330, the lows of early June 1994, then the psychological $1,300 region.
Resistance was expected at $1,357. But chartist William Adams of Rudolf Wolff regarded the market as bottoming-out, noting technical indicators have turned up and the market was oversold.
"I would look for a bounce in the next couple of days, or at least consolidation at these levels," he said.
In copper, prices failed to stray too far from either side of the $1,900 level after an early slide. It successively popped above the $1,900 parapet, but each time ducked back below.
It ended at $1,896, a $22 loss. "The close on copper certainly is not very encouraging," one trader said.

Nickel rechallenged the upside in the afternoon but it was capped by selling around $7,100 and $7,120. The market ended at $7,100, up $5, after getting a modest boost from news that WMC Ltd shut a mine in Western Australia after a miner was killed.
Lead finished slightly higher at $764, up $4.
Zinc closed the day a touch weaker at $1,018.50.

In New York, COMEX December gold ended down 40 cents at $382.70 an ounce, after trading in a $381.00-382.80 range. In bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted around $380.10, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $378.85, and the New York close Wednesday around $379.70. While sentiment remained bearish, analysts noted gold has bounced from the $370-380 level several times in the past three and a half years.

CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby contracts lower on aggressive fund selling, traders said. The market was seeking direction after Wednesday's late slide, led by a rumor Egypt had cancelled a cargo of U.S. wheat, traders said. Wheat futures closed 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower to three higher, with December down 2-1/2 at $4.20.

November crude succumbed to heating oil's pull by the end of the day after spending most of the session at or just below resistance at $24.65 a barrel, settling a sharp 76 cents higher at $24.81 a barrel. The rally in heating oil began with the first cool weather sweeping into the huge Northeastern heating oil market at a time when inventories in the region are the lowest they have been in a generation.

CSCE world sugar futures backed off yesterday's highs to settle lower on profit taking, but prices remained well-within their recent trading range. Producer pricing contributed to weakness in thin volume. The March contract settled 0.04 lower at 10.85, having ranged from 10.97 to 10.81. The back months settled 0.07 lower to 0.08 higher.
